Pan-cooked bulgur with vegetables
Chop the onion finely and dice the peppers and courgette; rinse the bulgur once and drain.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat and sauté the onion for 3 minutes until it turns translucent.
Add the peppers and courgette and stir for 4 minutes, until slightly softened.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the bulgur and stir for 1 minute to coat it in the oil.
Add the hot water, salt and thyme; when it boils, lower the heat and cook covered for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Take it off the heat, place a clean cloth under the lid and let it rest for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork and serve.
If you chop the vegetables to the same size, they cook in the same time.
You can use aubergine or mushrooms instead of courgette.
Serve hot with yoghurt or cacık.
Keeps 3 days in a closed container in the fridge; reheat with a sprinkle of water.
Eggy bread (French toast)
Half a teaspoon of cinnamon (optional)
Beat the eggs well with the milk and salt in a wide, flat dish; add cinnamon if you like it sweet.
Heat the pan over medium heat and melt half the butter.
Dip the bread slices in the mixture for 10 seconds so both sides soak; let the excess drip off.
Lay the slices in the pan and cook for 2–3 minutes until golden underneath.
Turn them, add the remaining butter around the edges and cook the other side for 2–3 minutes too.
Don’t turn the heat up too high, so the egg cooks through inside; drain on kitchen paper and serve hot.
Stale bread soaks up the mixture better and doesn’t fall apart.
For a savoury version add thyme and grated cheese.
Serve with tomatoes, cucumber and olives, or with fruit.
Eat straight away; it softens as it sits.
Cheesy potato rösti
50 g grated kashar cheese
Peel the potatoes and grate them coarsely; squeeze out the liquid well in a clean cloth.
Finely chop the spring onions.
Mix the potato, cheese, egg, spring onion, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, spread the mixture in the pan and flatten it with a spoon.
Cook covered for 7–8 minutes until browned underneath.
Turn it over using a plate and cook the other side for 5–6 minutes, until the potato is tender.
The better you squeeze the potatoes, the crispier the rösti.
Keep the heat medium; on high heat the outside burns while the inside stays raw.
Serve with yoghurt or a green salad.
Best eaten fresh; keep leftovers 1 day in the fridge and reheat in a pan.
